title: The Inspector's Letter
briefing: The Cold Chain Safety Authority has issued a formal finding: late data-logger downloads breach good distribution practice. Valtren has 28 days to submit a corrective action plan.
Ruth Adeyemi asks you to help write it.

evidence.title: The finding
evidence.body: Logger downloads late or missed at four depots; excursions detected after delivery. Severity: major. Repeat findings may lead to licence conditions.

evidence.title: Current status
evidence.body: Your control test identified the causes (no cover, no alert). Some depots have improved; two have not.

questions.prompt: What must the corrective action plan contain?

options.label: Root causes, actions with owners and dates, how effectiveness will be tested, and interim controls until then
options.feedback: What regulators look for: causes, actions, proof.

options.label: A clear commitment from the board to full compliance within 28 days, signed by the CEO
Refresher training for all depot staff on logger downloads, with attendance records and a quiz score kept as evidence
options.feedback: Treats a design gap as a knowledge gap.

questions.prompt: What interim control do you add while automation is built?

options.label: A daily central check of every depot's downloads, escalated to the depot manager by 10:00
options.feedback: Detective control with a clear owner and time limit.

options.label: A monthly compliance review of download records by Quality until automation is live
No interim control: automation is due in six weeks and a manual check would divert depot staff

questions.prompt: What tone do you take with the Authority?

options.label: Accept the finding, explain the causes you already found, and offer a progress meeting at 8 weeks
options.feedback: Shows a firm that knows and fixes its problems.

options.label: Accept most of it but challenge the 'major' rating, since no affected product reached a patient or a pharmacy
options.feedback: Disputing a well-evidenced finding damages trust.

options.label: Submit a complete plan on time and keep correspondence formal until the Authority responds
options.feedback: Adequate but misses a chance to build trust.

questions.prompt: What does this finding teach the business?

options.label: Control test results must be acted on quickly: the problem was known before the inspector found it
options.feedback: The cost of delay is now a formal finding.

options.label: The Authority's standard is stricter than the industry norm, so Valtren must plan for tougher inspections
Control test results should be handled through legal privilege so they do not become regulatory evidence
options.feedback: The opposite lesson; testing is how firms fix things before regulators find them.

lesson: A regulator's finding is a test of governance. Accept it, fix the causes with owners and dates, protect in the meantime, and act on your own test results sooner next time.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "The Inspector's Letter" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
